recipes.name: Ex-Girlfriend's Mom's Salsa Fresca (Pico de Gallo)
ingredients_raw: 1 jalapeno pepper, seeded and finely chopped - or more to taste
2.5 cups Roma (plum) tomatoes, seeded and chopped

steps.text: Mix red onion, jalapeño pepper, and lime juice in a bowl. Allow to stand for 5 minutes. Mix in tomatoes, cilantro, and salt; allow to stand 15 more minutes for flavors to blend.

raw_recipe.headline: Ex-Girlfriend's Mom's Salsa Fresca (Pico de Gallo)
raw_recipe.description: This salsa fresca recipe is a fresh-tasting combination of tomatoes, red onion, jalapeño, cilantro, and lime to serve with chips or your favorite Mexican dishes.

review.reviewBody: I made this earlier today but waited to really eat it until tonight so the flavors would meld together. There will be none of this left after tonight! I made it exactly as the recipe stated, using a red jalapeno (which I prefer) and kosher salt. The measurements are right on the money. This is great by the spoonful or as an accompaniment to something else. For those who aren't used to using jalapenos, be sure to read how to handle them, and know that each jalapeno has its own level of heat even by the kind of variety. So you may want to tread carefully. Thanks for the recipe!

Very good! I used 1/2 yellow onion, instead of red onion, and added 2 cloves garlic and 1/2 t. cumin, then pulsed in my Blendtec. Not hot; in fact, next time I'll add another jalapeno. It was even better the 2nd day.

Thank you for such a fantastic recipe! I brought this to work today for our Cinco de Mayo party. I got 1 1/2 quarts out of this recipe, and expected to take maybe half of it home. Nope. All gone except enough for about three chips by the end of the day, and everyone commented on how awesome it was. The only real change I made to it was to add some cumin, only because I love the flavor. I added it to taste, but if I had to guess, I'd say probably around a teaspoon. I also let the onion and peppers marinate for an hour before adding everything else, but that was more out of necessity with my schedule. I don't know if it made an actual difference. This was refrigerated over night before serving. This I do think made a difference. I tasted it 5 minutes after making it and was worried that it was way too hot for most people. By this morning, all the flavors had had time to blend, and the heat had mellowed.

AMAZING!!! Sometimes I use a white onion instead of red. Others suggest adding garlic, but I think it's perfect in it's "naked" state. I can eat this by the spoonful! A little trick to share: set the diced tomato in a colander and lightly salt, tossing occasionally. Drains the excess moisture from tomato and makes a much nicer pico (imho).

Recipe was good (as Modified): Cut down on lime (added last + to taste). Added 1 tsp garlic since it was obviously lacking that flavor. CAUTION: a bit too salty - try 1/2 tsp, taste first, then add more if you think it needs it. Otherwise, great. Will make again w these mods

I've been looking for a pico de gallo recipe that approximated Mexican restaurant salsa for years. This is the best one I've found. Awesome fresh taste and great texture. Just a few adjustments:

1. I use canned whole tomatoes, and then squish them by hand. More consistency, better texture and flavor than fresh, and you can usually get a 28 ounce can for about $1.
2. I use sliced jalapenos from a jar. Less work and they are already pickled. I pour some of the pickling liquid into the jalapenos and onions with the lime juice.
3. I taste the end product and sometimes add just a teaspoon of sugar to offset the bitterness of the lime juice. Makes a big difference.
4. I also make a double recipe, as we go through this stuff very quickly at my house!

This recipie was great! I used what I had at home which was 2x canned rotel tomatoes (drained the juice before adding), 1.5 lemon instead of lime, habanero pepper instead of jalapeños and himalayan salt . I blended the onion, lemon and pepper...let it sit...then added 1 can of rotel and salt, blended. I poured it into a different bowl and added the other can of drained rotel (for the slight chunkiness) and cilantro. Did I say yummmm already? Thanks for the recipe

Utilized fresh garden tomatoes and Vidalia onions. It tasted great fresh after I added more salt, minced garlic and onion powder to taste. I let it marinate over night. I had to add more salt and jalapenos as those flavors seemed to be have been absorbed overnight by the tomatoes. I had too much to eat fresh so I cold pack canned 5 pint jars. I tried a jar and it was "almost" as good as fresh.

This recipe is perfect, and I've made it many times. I use a little less salt, but that is just personal preference.

The reason I wrote this is that I recently went fishing and caught a few ocean whitefish. I had heard that this is a good fish for cevice but had never made cevice. After scouring the internet for cevice recipes, I didn't find one that looked great. So, I finally marinated the fish in lime and then mixed it in with this salsa fresca. It was the best cevice I've ever had.

I love this recipe as a basic salsa/pico recipe! Marinating the onions and chili make a big difference. I would use a hotter pepper like a serrano or habanero next time because the heat was lacking. Some Jalapeños are hotter than others, but generally they are a bit mild for my taste. I had to use lemon because I was out of limes and it was still super yummy. Would make again, for sure!
Everyone loved it! I did add more jalapeno and a teaspoon of sugar to balance the flavor. The tip about the onions being marinated was great it really mellows the raw onion flavor.
I don't necessarily measure anything just put in what I have around and taste. Nothing like fresh garden produce coming together.

I have used this recipe for years. We love it. I sometimes add a little garlic or garlic powder. Whatever doesn’t get eaten after a few days (I make a lot!) I have used in cheese sauce, chili, and potatoe soup

I made this exactly as written and found it to be okay, but I won't make it again. It was incredibly salty. I think the lime juice needs to be quantified with a standard measurement. I used two limes but they produced very little juice. I probably should have used two more. Overall, the finished product just wasn't memorable - except for being too salty and that's not the kind of memorable a recipe wants.
Was my first time to make Pico. Was perfect! This is definitely a fan favorite and I will probably make it several times a month. It’s great in scrambled eggs!
I used an unidentified pepper we had lying around instead of jalapeño, which made it a bit spicier, but the flavor mellowed out after sitting for a while.

I chop up roma tomatoes, put the salt on them, to let them sweat off their liquid. I drain the tomatoes, Pat them dry, then add the other ingredients. My husband won’t let me buy store bought pico de gallo anymore! He loves the lime flavor!
